# Canic 0.102 Implementation Status

Date: 2026-08-16

## Status

- State: B1 evidence is closed and remains approved as temporary conversion
  evidence. The maintainer rejected the unreleased dense `1..=991`
  condition-plus-handling register and simplified the implementation to four
  phases: Register, Map, Cut, then Clean and measure. All four phases are
  complete in the untagged `0.102.2` draft.
- Evidence baseline: clean `main` tag `v0.101.53` at
  `23c0328f78b215580d734ef01b52b35fa3e38ade`. The active constructor
  reconciliation is pinned separately to current-candidate control-plane/core
  source content at `0750c309104b111fa6f5a1b3355c04fcb38faf71`.
- Release boundary: 0.102 is reinstall-only and is not rolling-compatible with
  pre-0.102. Every Canic-owned canister in a Fleet must be installed from one
  admitted release set before activation; matching host/CLI callers and
  regenerated external bindings move with that boundary. Same-release retry,
  backup, restore and interruption recovery remain required.
- Design gate: the complete producer, dynamic-public-context and durable-state
  inventories remain accepted. The 991-row allocation and host metadata are
  superseded candidate evidence. The accepted review splits four of the 167
  mechanical buckets and yields 161 registered cause families plus ten local
  typed families. Count is evidence, not an acceptance target.
- Published checkpoints: `v0.102.0` at
  `e6dfd7d2d212f9fce4b1b16caba33d8062e3461d` and `v0.102.1` at
  `86763c5f16478e2e548e2059e5efaa963bf9a966`. They preserve reviewable B1
  evidence without representing incomplete diagnostic behavior as released.
- Review work remains in the existing untagged `0.102.2` changelog draft.
  The compact Rust/Candid wire, code-first internal model, typed mappings and
  host catalogue are implemented. The assignments remain unreleased and
  freely replaceable until the release; package version remains unchanged.
- Measurement gate: the retained v3 baseline passes and the targeted four-role
  closeout is recorded in [inventory.md](inventory.md#targeted-0102-closeout). It is
  role-scoped evidence, not a replacement retained audit.

## Implementation Phases

| Phase | Outcome | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Register | Review the 167 buckets by semantic cause and create `reasons.toml`, runtime constants and the host catalogue | Complete: 161 registered and ten local families |
| Map | Map typed failures at qualifying boundaries, keep local failures local and select explicit public projections | Complete |
| Cut | Make `InternalError` code-first and atomically replace the public wire across Rust, Candid, host, CLI and tests | Complete |
| Clean and measure | Remove dead prose and this frontier's tooling/authority, archive useful conversion evidence, touch only directly affected durable fields and record Wasm deltas | Complete: targeted four-role evidence recorded |

Historical B1/B2 labels below describe how the evidence was gathered. They are
not additional implementation phases or a permanent development workflow.

## Replacement Cause-Family Review

This is the accepted code-free Register review surface derived from B1
evidence. It mechanically groups the superseded 991
condition-plus-handling rows by semantic origin and canonical-condition
wording. The reviewed table, rather than the mechanical buckets, owns the
canonical cause-family decisions.

- `qualification` marks a possible global reason when B1 proves a public or
  masked boundary. Historical internal-only observations remain unresolved
  until review proves an operator, durable or machine boundary or keeps them
  local;
- `candidate` removes tuple dimensions and duplicated domain words, while
  `recommended_summary` is a generated hypothesis about common meaning;
- prior summaries and projections remain review evidence rather than
  reason-key dimensions; and
- every bucket must be accepted, renamed, merged, split or excluded before
  numbers are assigned. A bucket must split when one cause meaning,
  one semantic origin and one truthful summary cannot cover every qualifying
  producer. Optional guidance must be universally safe.

The review also resolves public projection. A masked exact identity receives a
global code only when it has an existing independently qualifying operator,
durable or machine consumer. Without one, the exact condition remains local
typed state and may map directly to a safe public registered reason. A true
operator-only reason has no public conversion. Public projection is explicit at
typed mapping or `InternalError` construction boundaries; there is no central
projection table. The generated `internal_only_review` token is unresolved
historical evidence, not a final category; review must resolve each such
producer to masked registered, operator-only, local typed or a non-diagnostic
disposition without creating observability infrastructure.

The source evidence has 166 canonical-condition buckets and 167
origin-qualified buckets. The initial qualification hints identified ten local
typed groups and 157 possible global buckets. Review split four mixed global
buckets, producing the accepted 161 registered and ten local cause families
across 171 rows. Sixty-eight buckets contain at least ten provisional
identities, 35 at least twenty, 16 at least fifty and four at least one hundred;
the largest contains 322. Those high-fan-in buckets require producer-by-producer
semantic review. The retained evidence pins `166 -> 167 -> 348 -> 572 -> 664
-> 991`, the provisional 157/10 qualification split and the final 161/10
review outcome.

Count is review evidence only. Maintainer review accepts the register; count
neither accepts nor rejects it and never permits unrelated causes to collapse.

### Semantic Review Decisions

The table below is the producer-level review. `global` means the exact cause has
a proved qualifying boundary. `local` means the typed exact condition receives
no global identity; it may still map directly to the safe registered public
reason named in the projection column. `boundary_review` means semantic
grouping is settled but an existing qualifying boundary still needs proof. It
never authorizes new observability infrastructure. `public_as_is` is a reviewed
safe identity; any other projection names the safe public reason required at
that boundary, not proof that the exact condition itself qualifies.

The granular pass above remains migration evidence, but it is not allocation
authority. It split the canonical cause families by subsystem, field, phase and
safe public target, reproducing producer-level identity under different names.
The accepted Register review below restores the design rule: handling,
projection, producer, subsystem, role, endpoint, phase, function and source
location do not normally split a reason. Each row exactly partitions one
mechanical cause family. Public treatment is intentionally absent from this
table; public-as-is and safe projection choices are explicit at their typed
mapping boundaries and have no central projection table.

## Superseded B2 Candidate

The candidate proved the following scaffolding and absence properties. Its
991-row taxonomy is not the accepted allocation:

1. lossless raw identities and registered reason identities are distinct and
   format only as compact unpadded `E<decimal>`;
2. all candidate rows have one canonical runtime declaration and no local alias
   or second numeric construction path;
3. all 991 provisional rows and zero retired rows are represented consistently
   in the candidate host ledger with complete typed catalogue metadata;
4. the native registered inventory, ledger, host catalogue and generated JSON
   are bijective, while retirement and never-allocated lookup remain distinct;
5. `canic diagnostic` accepts only raw decimal or exact uppercase-prefixed
   input and renders typed known, retired or unknown outcomes;
6. canister-reachable source imports no host ledger, JSON, review frontier or
   producer-to-code map; and
7. representative Component, Fleet Subnet Root and Wasm Store release
   artifacts contain none of those complete host-only assets.

## Archived Typed Preparation

The first preparatory slice replaced `AccessError::Denied(String)` and
`AccessErrorKind` with 26 finite direct access failures plus a transparent
typed internal cause. Its provisional exact/public pairs were inputs to the
subsequent semantic review and have since been regenerated from the accepted
161-reason register. The repository-atomic public cut is now complete.

The first Store slice maps all 13 finite `TemplateManifestOpsError` variants
and 12 finite publication variants to provisional exact/public identities.
Publication binding/cardinality/write-fence branches are typed, the combined
GC-fence-or-release-missing predicate is split, and broad GC/transport wrappers
are prevented from selecting a generic identity until their exact cuts.
